strings.hist_tagline: Four thousand years on Albay Gulf, from the fishing village of Sawangan to the regional capital of Bicol.
strings.hist_brief_title: The Story of Legazpi, in Brief
strings.hist_brief1_desc: Archaeological evidence from the Mataas Shell Scoop and Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave proves early trade across the Pacific.
strings.hist_brief2_desc: The 1814 Mayon eruption separated inland Albay Nuevo and coastal Binanuahan, creating the dual-center urban layout seen today.
strings.hist_brief3_desc: Legazpi earned city charters in 1892 (Becerra Law), 1948 (RA 306), and definitively on June 12, 1959 under Republic Act 2234.
strings.hist_tl1_desc: Earliest archaeological artifact in Albay Gulf; ancient seafaring networks.
strings.hist_tl2_desc: Franciscans establish the first chapel dedicated to St. Gregory the Great.
strings.hist_tl3_desc: Elevated to capital of the sprawling Partido de Ibalón colonial province.
strings.hist_tl4_desc: 1,200 casualties; survivors rebuild Albay Nuevo inland and Binanuahan on the coast.
strings.hist_tl5_desc: Royal Decree officially christens the town; Don Lorenzo Hao becomes 1st Gobernadorcillo.
strings.hist_tl6_desc: First city status uniting Legazpi Port, Albay, and Daraga into one Ayuntamiento.
strings.hist_tl7_desc: Fierce Philippine-American War action at San Rafael Bridge led by Gen. Paua.
strings.hist_tl8_desc: U.S. 158th RCT and Bicolano guerrillas liberate the ruined port district.
strings.hist_tl9_desc: Permanent cityhood chartered; Mayor Ramon A. Arnaldo serves as first city mayor.
strings.hist_tl10_desc: Presidential Decree No. 1 designates Legazpi the administrative hub of Region V.
strings.hist_tl11_desc: Pioneering first permanent provincial disaster risk reduction office in the nation.
strings.hist_tl12_desc: Modern international gateway opens; commercial expansion accelerates.
strings.hist_tl13_desc: Mayor Hisham Ismail leads push toward Highly Urbanized City status.
